prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: EN · Plan comparison (language en).
Grid: 5 columns × 6 rows. Row headers: none declared.
Per-column content facts (content px at 17px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "Feature" · longest unbreakable word 63px · one-line width 93px
  col 2: header "Free" · longest unbreakable word 88px · one-line width 88px
  col 3: header "Pro" · longest unbreakable word 73px · one-line width 73px
  col 4: header "Enterprise" · longest unbreakable word 83px · one-line width 255px
  col 5: header "Notes" · longest unbreakable word 81px · one-line width 465px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 643px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 642px.
Fixed: content, font, 17px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

The image shows the table's content with every cell on one line, so you can read everything. Study it first.
1) Understand it: what is the table for, how will people read, scan and compare it, which columns play the same or similar role, which values must stay intact, which text may wrap naturally, and where existing row height could absorb wrapping.
2) Propose 3 genuinely different column-width designs for 643px (different strategies, not small variations).
Reply ONLY JSON: {"understanding":{"purpose":"","reading":"","groups":["columns that belong together and why"],"keep_intact":[""],"may_wrap":[""]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[int px per column, column 1 first],"idea":"one sentence"}]}

log.raw: {"understanding":{"purpose":"Compare Free, Pro, and Enterprise plan capabilities feature by feature, with Notes supplying caveats and context.","reading":"Readers scan down the Feature labels, then compare across the three plan columns; Notes is read afterward as supporting detail.","groups":["Free, Pro, and Enterprise belong together as parallel plan-value columns and should remain easy to compare.","Feature is the row-label column and anchors each comparison.","Notes is a separate explanatory column and should not compete with the plan values."],"keep_intact":["Headers: Feature, Free, Pro, Enterprise, Notes","Short plan values such as Unlimited, Community, 30 days, 1 year, and Custom","Tokens such as SSO / SAML and 24/7","Numeric units such as 2 GB and 100 GB"],"may_wrap":["Notes prose","The long Enterprise support phrase at word boundaries","Multi-word Feature labels if necessary"]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[112,112,104,150,163],"idea":"Balance the three plan columns for quick comparison while giving Notes enough width to wrap to only a few lines."},{"name":"B","widths":[104,112,100,116,209],"idea":"Prioritize the explanatory Notes column and the short tier values, accepting heavier wrapping in the long Enterprise support cell."},{"name":"C","widths":[150,110,100,110,171],"idea":"Give the Feature row labels generous space and keep the plan columns as compact, comparable value slots with moderate Notes width."}]}
